aspect_catalog.label: Requirements and product fit
aspect_catalog.prompt: Does the change satisfy the user request without scope drift?

aspect_catalog.label: Core logic
aspect_catalog.prompt: Are the main algorithms, data flow, and invariants correct?

aspect_catalog.label: Edge cases and contracts
aspect_catalog.prompt: Do boundary values, empty inputs, errors, concurrency, and API contracts hold?

aspect_catalog.label: Tests and regressions
aspect_catalog.prompt: Do tests prove the changed behavior and relevant failure paths?

aspect_catalog.label: Security, privacy, and secrets
aspect_catalog.prompt: Are auth, secrets, private data, injection, paths, and dependencies safe?

aspect_catalog.label: LLM and tool trust boundaries
aspect_catalog.prompt: Are model/tool outputs treated as untrusted and are external actions bounded?

aspect_catalog.label: Data integrity, encoding, migrations, and backcompat
aspect_catalog.prompt: Are stored data, encodings, formats, migrations, and old outputs preserved?

aspect_catalog.label: Integration, runtime, reliability, and cleanup
aspect_catalog.prompt: Does this work in the real runtime with correct resource cleanup and retries?

aspect_catalog.label: Observability, logs, metrics, and debuggability
aspect_catalog.prompt: Can failures be diagnosed without leaking secrets or hiding root causes?

aspect_catalog.label: Performance, cost, and scalability
aspect_catalog.prompt: Does the change avoid avoidable slow paths, duplicate work, and waste?

aspect_catalog.label: UX, UI, accessibility, and i18n
aspect_catalog.prompt: Does the user-facing behavior remain clear, reachable, and language-safe?

aspect_catalog.label: Developer experience, docs, API, and examples
aspect_catalog.prompt: Would a maintainer or caller know how to use and verify this change?

aspect_catalog.label: Release, deploy, rollback, and CI
aspect_catalog.prompt: Are deployment, CI, rollback, and versioning implications handled?

aspect_catalog.label: Domain-specific risk and compliance
aspect_catalog.prompt: Are domain rules, client data, legal/business constraints, and project policies respected?

aspect_passes.notes: Stage 5 stays code-only, default-deny, and stops before remote/mobile Stage 6 or live Windows changes.
Default deny, enforcement-vs-UX separation, atomic desired commit and bounded recovery invariants reviewed and fixed.
Cancellation, crash windows, expiry, rollback, duplicate evidence, future evidence, and retry failures have regressions.
All seven Stage 5 harnesses are in guard.sln; 85 scoped and 321 total safe checks pass.
Proxy override, SID/session binding, signature provenance, replay floors, opaque child payloads, and audit outbox issues fixed.
Only source builds and fake/pure harnesses ran; no Guard or Windows enforcement action executed.
Signature envelope intentionally versioned to v2 before production; canonical UTF-8 bytes and exact digests are covered.
Atomic reconcile intent and idempotent audit dispatch/ack close cancellation and hard-crash gaps in the ports.
Every successful, rejected, rate-limited, and dependency outcome has a durable, idempotent audit intent.
Bounded inputs, catalogs, policy scopes, evidence sets, and serialized single-writer reconciliation avoid unbounded work.
No rendered UI changed; website request readiness fails closed when extension UX is missing, cross-session, stale, future, or unhealthy.
Public contracts document trust boundaries, atomicity, delivery idempotency, and production adapter obligations.
No production wiring or deployment changed; code is isolated for commit/revert and VM gates remain explicit.
No secrets, client data, HTTPS interception, live policy changes, or child-authoritative identity paths were introduced.

scores.reasons: Twelve P1/P2 issues were fixed: browser override precedence, proxy/child identity, replay/signature provenance, enforcement/UX split, atomic request and desired-state outboxes, cancellation/crash recovery, session/future evidence, solution coverage, and durable idempotent audit.
scores.verification_summary: Final Release warn-as-error build: 0 warnings/errors; 321/321 safe checks; 85/85 Stage 5 scoped checks; NuGet vulnerability audit clean; three independent final reviews accept with no remaining P0-P2.
